text.tspan: STATBELT Utility- Hypothesis Testing Means for Raw Data
To conduct a hypothesis test for a mean using STATBELT Utility and raw data, follow the path:
Tests → Inference for Means → One sample → Hypothesis test.
Under “Where is the data?” choose “Column data from the main spreadsheet,” then choose the
Type the mean from the null hypothesis into “Hypothesized mean μ₀.”
Under “Type of test,” choose Left-tailed (<), Right-tailed (>), or Two-tailed (≠).
Type the significance level α. The results appear as soon as you type.
The output from STATBELT will include the sample mean, the test statistic, and the P-Value, all computed
Example 11: Hypothesis Testing Means from Raw Data
According to a 2017 study conducted by Inside Higher Education, the average high school grade point
average at that time was 3.3. A random sample of grade point averages from 48 high school and college
A student advocacy group believes the claimed grade point average is too high. Test the claim that the
mean grade point average of high school students is less than 3.3 using significance level 0.05.
A college professor believes that high school grade point averages have been inflated, and that college
grade point averages are lower than high school grade point averages. Test the claim that college grade point
averages are lower than 3.3 using 0.05 level of significance. You can copy the
: High School and College Grade Point Averages
The first claim is made about high school students. The claim is that high school grade point
averages are lower than 3.3, which was the claim made by Inside Higher Education.
